summary: "War of the Coprophages" is the third episode written by Darin Morgan, following "Humbug" and "Clyde Bruckman's Final Repose." The note describes production details: the show used around three hundred cockroaches, detailed rubber cockroach props, and "piles and piles" of faux-dung to create the effect of a cockroach infestation. It also explains the title's reference to H.G. Wells and the character Dr. Berenbaum's namesake.
one_line: Darin Morgan's third episode, "War of the Coprophages," with its cockroach-infestation production details and title and character namesakes.
key_facts: "War of the Coprophages" was Darin Morgan's third episode.
"Humbug" was the episode that came before "War of the Coprophages" in Darin Morgan's run, and it aired in the second season.
"Clyde Bruckman's Final Repose" was a season three episode and came before "War of the Coprophages" in Darin Morgan's run.
To achieve the effect of a cockroach infestation, the show used around three hundred cockroaches for the episode.
The episode used extremely detailed rubber cockroach props in addition to live cockroaches.
The episode used "piles and piles" of faux-dung.
The episode's title is a reference to the novel "The War of the Worlds" by H.G. Wells.
The episode's title also references the 1938 radio adaptation of "The War of the Worlds" by Orson Welles.
The character Dr. Berenbaum is named for entomologist May Berenbaum.
